chunks: Safwan, from Al-Ays ibn Al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who bought a slave who had children from a free woman, so he emancipated him. He said: The guardianship (walā’) of his children is for the one who emancipated him.
ai.seo_question: Who inherits the right of manumission (walā') for a slave who has children from a free woman?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the application of 'walā’ al-‘itq' (right of manumission) for an 'umm al-walad' (a slave mother of a child by her master), ruling that the patronage rights belong to the master who frees her. This establishes a direct link between the act of emancipation and the resulting social and inheritance bonds, distinct from the mother's free lineage. The ruling underscores the importance of manumission in Islamic jurisprudence as a means of integrating freed slaves into the patron's family structure.
